version.changelog: Refreshed this Chinese scene skill to align its shared setup, API-key, upload, and command guidance with the latest official sparki-video-editor skill while preserving its scenario-specific positioning.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: video-resizer-zh
Version: 1.0.10

The video-resizer-zh skill bundle is a legitimate integration for the Sparki AI video editing service. The CLI tool (sparki_cli) uses standard libraries like httpx and typer to interact with the official API at agent-api.sparki.io for video processing tasks. The SKILL.md instructions provide clear guidance for the AI agent on how to handle user requests, manage API keys, and orchestrate the video editing workflow without any evidence of malicious intent, unauthorized data access, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requested access are consistent with a Sparki video-resizer CLI: it only needs a Sparki API key, reads/writes an OpenClaw-scoped config/workspace, and talks to agent-api.sparki.io; nothing obvious is disproportionate or unrelated to the stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description target Sparki video resizing and the package contains a Sparki CLI implementation (upload, edit, status, download). The declared primary credential (SPARKI_API_KEY), filesystem permissions (read $CWD, write ~/.openclaw/config and workspace sparki/videos), and network domain (agent-api.sparki.io) align with a tool that uploads video files and talks to a Sparki backend. There are no unrelated credentials or strange external services requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md gives explicit step-by-step commands (sparki setup, upload, edit, status, download) and limits upload methods to local paths or a Telegram Mini App link. The instructions reference only the declared env var (SPARKI_API_KEY) and the local config/workspace paths. They do instruct the agent to read local files the user points to and to store the API key in the local config — both expected for a CLI that uploads and downloads videos.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package includes full Python source (pyproject.toml and src/sparki_cli) and the SKILL.md metadata mentions running 'uv sync' (and required binary 'uv'). There is no external download-from-URL or opaque installer in the manifest. 'uv' is an uncommon required binary in public packages — this is not inherently malicious but is an unusual dependency; the install approach is internal/packaged rather than fetching arbitrary code from random URLs, which lowers risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only SPARKI_API_KEY is the primary credential; an optional SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK env var is supported. No other tokens/secrets are requested. The number and nature of env vars are proportionate to a service that authenticates to a third-party API and optionally customizes upload link/base URL.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-on, is user-invocable, and may run autonomously per platform defaults (disable-model-invocation:false) which is normal. It writes only to its own config under ~/.openclaw and a workspace path for video outputs. It does not modify other skills or system-wide configs beyond its own config directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: a Sparki CLI for uploading, editing, and downloading videos using a Sparki API key. Before installing: (1) Confirm you trust the Sparki service (agent-api.sparki.io) since video files and your API key are sent there. (2) The skill will store the API key in ~/.openclaw/config/sparki.json (or read SPARKI_API_KEY from the environment) — avoid putting highly privileged keys there if you want to limit exposure. (3) The package requires an unusual binary named 'uv' for its declared install step — verify what 'uv' is in your environment before running it. (4) The skill will read local files you point it to and write output into ~/.openclaw/workspace/sparki/videos; review and isolate if you are concerned about sensitive content. If you want higher safety, run the CLI in an isolated environment (container or dedicated VM) and use a limited Sparki API key.
